heard: Voyager 2 launched two weeks before its twin, yet was named second. Most people assume the lower-numbered spacecraft must have lifted off first. In 1977, NASA utilized a rare planetary alignment occurring once every 176 years. Voyager 1 took a shorter and faster path to reach Jupiter and Saturn sooner. Meanwhile, Voyager 2 was sent on a longer journey toward the edge of the solar system. That detour made it the only spacecraft to ever visit the ice giants, Uranus and Neptune. It discovered rings and new moons before diving south and entering interstellar space in 2018. Reaching its destination second is why Voyager 2 launched two weeks before its twin, yet was named second.
